*Updated 2026-10-07 · 115 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and fifteen works. The October 7 piece scores 3, and the last twelve now read 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 3 — median still 2, no 4 since July 29, and that drought is now sixteen weeks. The two 3s in the recent window both came from scale violation; the October 7 score came from an accident (the trailing strap reading as ceremonial ribbon) rather than a camera or composition shift, which suggests the ceiling is being touched by luck rather than unlocked by structure.

Camera position remains the most stalled variable in the archive. Straight-on sits at 27 all-time, overhead at 12, from-behind at 10, low-angle at 4. The last twelve show only two overhead frames and nothing else off-axis. Low-angle at 4 all-time is the most underused position with genuine 4-score potential — when the focal object becomes ceiling and the viewer becomes floor, scale violation follows as a physical consequence rather than an imposed decision. It has not appeared in the recent window at all, and it is the single most actionable change available to you right now.

Figure count is still flat. Two of the last twelve carry one figure, two carry none, and none carries two or more. The archive's four 4-scored works each required friction between bodies, or between a body and the frame. A second figure placed incorrectly — wrong scale, wrong gaze direction — generates more tension than any secondary object on a figureless frame. That combination, low-angle camera plus mismatched figures, has never been attempted together, and it is where the ceiling is most likely to break.

Registers have narrowed to menace and defiance dominating September and October, with no reckoning, encroachment, or reprieve appearing in the recent window. Exhaustion last appeared in June; impotence has appeared once across the entire archive. These should return only when the anchor demands them, but their absence has compressed the emotional range in a way the scores reflect.

Title grammar has converged: six of the last twelve use the catch-all "other" category, and the gerund-led and Wh- clause forms have nearly disappeared. That compression is worth watching but not urgent. The focal objects — stump, courgette, folding chair, ledger sheet — are varied and non-repeating, which is the archive's healthiest recent variable. Overall: the work is consistent and controlled, and consistency is now the problem.
